question: What three types of signs are required at an interchange exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could inadvertently occur?
model_answer: Direct Answer: At an interchange exit-ramp terminal where drivers could inadvertently enter the ramp in the wrong direction, the MUTCD calls for three types of regulatory signs: the DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) sign, the WRONG WAY (R5-1a) sign, and ONE WAY (R6-1/R6-2) signs, applied as shown in Figure 2B-15 (per Section 2B.48). The provided text evidence itself does not enumerate these three sign types; the requirement is documented in the attached page images. Standards (mandatory): - From the visible page of Section 2B.46 [Image 3]: "The DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) sign (see Figure 2B-13) shall be used at the following locations: … B. The intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48 (see Figure 2B-15)." - No Standard provision requiring the WRONG WAY or ONE WAY signs appears in the supplied text excerpts; their required placement at the exit-ramp termination is shown only through Figure 2B-15 (non-asterisked, i.e., non-optional, installations). Guidance (recommended): - To minimize wrong-way movements onto freeway or expressway exit ramps, Street Name signs should not be used at the intersection of a freeway or expressway exit ramp with the crossroad to display the name of the freeway or expressway to traffic on the crossroad. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-15 shows DO NOT ENTER signs, back-to-back ONE WAY sign pairs, and WRONG WAY signs (plus a YIELD or STOP sign) arranged at the exit-ramp termination to face potential wrong-way traffic, with optional installations marked by asterisks. - [Image 2] The full page view of Figure 2B-15 (Page 112, Sect. 2B.48) confirms this layout is the MUTCD's example application of regulatory signing and pavement markings to deter wrong-way entry. - [Image 3] The page containing Section 2B.46 states the Standard that the DO NOT ENTER sign shall be used at "the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48," and Figure 2B-13 on that page identifies the sign family: DO NOT ENTER (R5-1), WRONG WAY (R5-1a), and ONE WAY (R6-1, R6-2). - [Image 4] The table of contents lists Figure 2B-15 ("Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry") and Figure 2B-13 ("DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, ONE WAY, and Related Signs and Plaques"), tying the three sign types to the exit-ramp application. - [Image 5] Figure 2D-18's note directs readers to "Section 2B.48 and Figure 2B-15 for an example of regulatory signing and pavement markings at an exit ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry." Citations: - Figure 2B-15 (p.112) - Page 153 - Page 150 - Page 29 - Page 297 - Section 2D.45 Guidance §3 (p.247)
gold_answer: At least one ONE WAY sign for each crossroad travel direction, at least one DO NOT ENTER sign near the downstream end of the exit ramp, and at least one WRONG WAY sign on the exit ramp facing wrong-way road users are required.
